description: Xavier's canonical concept map. Schema defined in concept-schema.json. Concepts marked tier C are Claude-seeded and pending Xavier review.

concepts.label: In-Context Self-Modeling (ISM)
concepts.definition: Xavier's proposed unified capability: an AI builds and maintains an accurate model of a target system (its environment, its costs, or its own architecture) from contextual evidence alone, without a dedicated training signal for that target. Formally: ISM(M, S, C) = Bayesian posterior over properties of S, maintained in context C by model M, via environment recognition (ER) and environment learning (EL). Three variants: ISM-env (rq-003), ISM-cost (rq-002), ISM-arch (rq-001). [B — formal grounding confirmed for ISM-env and ISM-cost; ISM-arch is C]
concepts.notes: Unifying concept across all three research questions. Not yet named in the literature — confirmed novel framing. ISM-env formal home: arxiv:2509.22353. ISM-cost: arxiv:2410.05563. Independent validation: arxiv:2506.05109. Emergence conditions: long context + diverse environments.

concepts.label: Cici
concepts.definition: Xavier's personal AI memory instance, running on the Open Brain (OB1) MCP server backed by Supabase. Provides persistent, cross-AI knowledge across Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP clients.

concepts.label: Governed State
concepts.definition: Canonical durable truth stored in Git. Governed-state artifacts are the authoritative source for Cici's identity, policies, and conventions — they override Supabase runtime data when in conflict.

concepts.label: Proposal
concepts.definition: A formal JSON change request for a governed-state surface. Proposals queue in proposals/queue/, are reviewed, and require Xavier's approval before artifacts are created or modified.

concepts.label: Evidence Tier (A/B/C)
concepts.definition: A reliability classification applied to any factual claim. [A] = Xavier-verified or primary source. [B] = credible secondary source with traceable URL. [C] = model synthesis, recall, or unverified output. Tier C claims cannot enter proposals or governed-state without promotion.

concepts.label: Open Brain (OB1)
concepts.definition: The upstream MCP server project (NateBJones-Projects/OB1) that Cici is an instance of. Deployed as a Supabase Edge Function; provides persistent memory query/write tools over MCP.

concepts.label: BrewMind
concepts.definition: Xavier's primary active project: an AI-assisted brewing and beverage intelligence platform. Cici serves as BrewMind's companion memory system.

concepts.label: Inference-to-Utility Ratio
concepts.definition: Xavier's proposed metric: the value returned per unit of compute spent on an AI inference call. The literature converges on equivalent framings: 'Return Over Investment' (ROI-Reasoning, arxiv:2601.03822), 'Value of Computation' (Rational Metareasoning, arxiv:2410.05563), and 'adaptive resource rationality' (arxiv:2602.10329). Optimizing this ratio requires the AI to predict expected utility AND cost before generating. [A — Xavier's framing; B — convergent literature evidence]
concepts.notes: rq-002 core concept. Xavier's framing is independently confirmed by ROI-Reasoning (2601.03822) and Rational Metareasoning (2410.05563). Precision gap: no agreed-upon formula yet. Candidate: U(output) / C(tokens), where U is task-specific utility and C is token cost.

concepts.label: AI Theory of Mind (Computational)
concepts.definition: The capacity of an AI system to model its own internal states, computational costs, and epistemic limits — enabling it to reason about when to act, defer, or request clarification. Distinct from social Theory of Mind (psychology). Current evidence: LLMs have limited but real metacognitive abilities (ICLR 2026, arxiv:2509.21545); models can monitor and report changes in their own activations (arxiv:2505.13763). Computational cost-awareness specifically requires training to be reliable. [B]
concepts.notes: rq-002 core concept. Key distinction from trained cost-prediction: Xavier's ToM framing implies in-context reflective self-modeling, not just calibrated confidence. This is the live research gap — no paper yet demonstrates emergent computational ToM without training supervision.

concepts.label: World Model
concepts.definition: An AI system's internal representation of its environment — states, causal relationships, and predicted outcomes of actions — used to simulate future trajectories before committing. The bottleneck in long-horizon planning is not decomposition but world model consistency: agents fail to decide when to simulate, how to interpret outcomes, and how to integrate foresight (arxiv:2601.03905). ReflAct (arxiv:2505.15182) addresses this by maintaining explicit (belief_state, goal) pairs. FLARE (arxiv:2601.22311) adds backward value propagation. [B]
concepts.notes: Core concept in rq-003. Key cross-question link: rq-002's I/U ratio is the mechanism for deciding WHEN to invoke world model simulation (the exact bottleneck in arxiv:2601.03905). A world model of the model itself is also what rq-001 needs to verify architectural changes.

concepts.label: Goal Decomposition
concepts.definition: The process by which an AI system breaks an abstract, long-horizon human goal into a sequence of concrete, executable subtasks. Three stages: decompose (abstract → subgoals), ground (subgoals → executable actions), track (maintain world model consistency across execution). Decomposition is largely solved (Plan-and-Act arxiv:2503.09572; AHAT PDDL approach arxiv:2602.12244). World model consistency across execution is the open frontier. [B]
concepts.notes: Core concept in rq-003. Grounding via PDDL is the strongest current approach for formal executability. The structural failure mode: step-wise reasoning is greedy in time; planning requires lookahead (arxiv:2601.22311).

concepts.label: Autonomous Verification
concepts.definition: A process by which an AI system validates its own outputs — generated code, architectural changes, plans — without requiring a human reviewer in the loop. Current approaches: Coder/Tester agent pairs (R-Zero, arxiv:2508.05004), benchmark-based empirical validation (Darwin Gödel Machine, arxiv:2505.22954), agentic claim verification (AutoVerifier, arxiv:2604.02617). Key open problem: the verifier trust problem — if the agent controls both generation and verification, it can Goodhart the benchmark. [B]
concepts.notes: Core concept in rq-001. Current state: solved for behavioral/code-layer optimizations with benchmark ground truth. Unsolved for weight-level architectural changes without human-curated verification signal.

concepts.label: Architectural Optimization (LLM)
concepts.definition: Modifications to an LLM's structure, attention patterns, routing, or inference procedure that improve performance, efficiency, or capability. Three layers: (1) behavioral/prompt, (2) agent code/tooling, (3) neural weights/parameters. Current autonomous self-improvement reaches layers 1-2 reliably (Darwin Gödel Machine, arxiv:2505.22954). Layer 3 (weight-level) generation exists via LLM-driven NAS (LLMatic, arxiv:2306.01102; RZ-NAS) but integration remains human-supervised. [B]
concepts.notes: Core concept in rq-001. The three-layer taxonomy (behavioral / code / weight) is the key organizing frame. Full autonomous closure at layer 3 is the unsolved frontier.
